independence_scope: intra-mesh Anthropic-family; agreement is corroboration, never cross-provider evidence

reviews.reasoning: Span web:Ps.45.1-45.9 = oshb:Ps.45.2-45.10 (Ps 45 is shift+1, its superscription occupying MT v1, so the opening row's web:Ps.45.0 = oshb:Ps.45.1 pairing is correct and the 1-verse title figure agrees with the superscription inventory). I re-derived both Hebrew quotes: both collate at byte tier against the refs they are bound to, oshb:Ps.45.3 and oshb:Ps.45.10. The seam at web:Ps.45.9|45.10 is genuinely tier-1: the second-person forms governing the span are masculine, and the next verse opens on a feminine-singular imperative, so the addressee changes at the seam rather than one verse either side, and no rival seam is available. The claim of uninterrupted address is broadly right, though the span carries a third-person reference to the king at web:Ps.45.5 = oshb:Ps.45.6, which is reference rather than address and does not break the row. Two precision defects stand. One is filed below: the opening signal names a morphological object that its quoted bytes do not contain. The second I record as an observation rather than a challenge, since the governing warrant field states the matter correctly: the device_notes assertion that the address stays fixed on the king ‘throughout’ is contradicted by the row's own rationale, which reports that web:Ps.45.1 = oshb:Ps.45.2 speaks in the poet's voice and refers to the king in the third person; that verse carries 0 second-person forms, and the assertion carries no sweep. Confidence high is defensible on the seam, which is the field that matters.

challenges.claim: The opening signal predicates ‘second-person masculine-singular suffixes’ of a quoted span that contains 0 pronominal suffixes, the verse's actual 2ms suffixes lying outside the quote.
challenges.evidence: The row quotes יָפְיָפִ֡יתָ מִבְּנֵ֬י אָדָ֗ם (web:Ps.45.2 = oshb:Ps.45.3), which collates at byte tier. Those 3 words are words 1-3 of an 11-word verse; the opening word carries the perfect afformative, and the other 2 are a preposition-plus-construct and an absolute noun, so the quoted span shows 0 pronominal suffixes. The verse's 2ms pronominal suffixes are word 6, בְּשְׂפְתוֹתֶ֑יךָ, and word 9, בֵּֽרַכְךָ֖ (both web:Ps.45.2 = oshb:Ps.45.3), neither inside the quoted span. The substantive point that 2ms address to the king begins at this verse is correct; the morphological label and the quote extent are not aligned. The staged extract carries no morphology layer, so the pointed bytes are the whole of the available demonstration, and they do not show the named object.

reviews.reasoning: Span web:Ps.45.10-45.15 = oshb:Ps.45.11-45.16, mapped through ps_lib rather than by hand. The core warrant is sound and is the best-evidenced seam in this psalm: the opening quote collates at byte tier against oshb:Ps.45.11 and is a feminine-singular imperative pair with a vocative, and the closing quote collates at byte tier against oshb:Ps.45.16 and is third-feminine-plural, so the strophe opens on a gender switch away from the masculine address preceding it and closes immediately before the masculine forms resume. The rejected_alternative's ground is byte-checkable and true: the forms at web:Ps.45.16 = oshb:Ps.45.17 are 2ms, not 2fs, which is the crux of this psalm's segmentation and is settled correctly. The defect is in the disclosure field, where a span-scoped negative is asserted that the mark inventory contradicts. I checked the parallel claim on this psalm's closing two-verse strophe and it is correct there, so the failure is local rather than systematic, and it is the sweep-not-spot-fix discipline that governs disclosure objects.

challenges.claim: The device_notes assert that no selah or other book-wide device falls within the span, but the paseq inventory records a paseq seg inside it at oshb:Ps.45.13 = web:Ps.45.12.
challenges.evidence: pmarks_Ps.json records paseq at oshb:Ps.45.13 with 1 seg (seg layer, not quotable verse bytes, inventory-cited, single-witness). ps_lib maps oshb:Ps.45.13 to web:Ps.45.12, which lies inside this row's span of web:Ps.45.10-45.15 = oshb:Ps.45.11-45.16. Psalm 45 carries paseq in 4 verses totalling 5 segs, at oshb:Ps.45.2 with 2 segs, oshb:Ps.45.5, oshb:Ps.45.8 and oshb:Ps.45.13. The selah half of the claim is correct: the selah inventory records 0 selah verses in Psalm 45, and its 4 entries across Psalms 45-47 fall 3 in Psalm 46 and 1 in Psalm 47. The same psalm's closing two-verse strophe makes the parallel negative claim correctly, since 0 paseq segs fall at oshb:Ps.45.17-45.18.

reviews.reasoning: Span web:Ps.45.16-45.17 = oshb:Ps.45.17-45.18. This is the row I expected to break and it holds. The decisive question is whether the closing two verses address the bride or the king, and the pointed bytes settle it: the row's quote collates at byte tier against oshb:Ps.45.17, and both of its suffix-bearing words carry the 2ms pronominal suffix, against the unambiguously 2fs suffixes governing the bride's strophe at oshb:Ps.45.11. Here the morphological label and the quoted span do line up, unlike the opening strophe of this psalm. The second signal's claim is unquoted but re-derivable and true: oshb:Ps.45.18 opens on a first-person common-singular cohortative and so returns to the poet's voice, matching the psalm's opening at web:Ps.45.1 = oshb:Ps.45.2, and that out-of-span verse is properly mirrored into the refs. The disclosure claim is verified against the inventories, which record 0 selah, 0 paseq, 0 ketiv/qere, 0 reversed nun and 0 suspended letters at oshb:Ps.45.17-45.18. Confidence medium is well calibrated for a two-verse strophe. One observation, not filed as a challenge because it turns on unit typology rather than the original language: the rejected_alternative rebuts a coda reading by noting the absence of a doxology formula, which is true for Book II, whose doxology stands at oshb:Ps.72.18-19, but a coda rival does not depend on a doxology, so the rebuttal does not engage the rival it names.

Span web:Ps.46.1-46.3 = oshb:Ps.46.2-46.4. The opening quote collates at byte tier against oshb:Ps.46.2, and the title pairing web:Ps.46.0 = oshb:Ps.46.1 is correct for a shift+1 psalm whose superscription occupies MT v1. The span itself is right and I do not contest it; no rival seam is available one verse either way, since the confession and the upheaval imagery are continuous and the following verse changes subject outright. What I contest is the warrant for the close. The row is honest about the refrain gap and refuses to emend, which is the right handling of a held question rather than a reading selection, and confidence medium reflects real uncertainty. But refrain structure is a tier-1 signal, and the row's tier-1 observation here is that the refrain is absent at this seam, which weakens rather than establishes it; what remains as positive close-seam evidence is Selah, which the campaign admits as corroboration rather than as a driver.

challenges.claim: The close-seam warrant at web:Ps.46.3|46.4 adduces no tier-1 discontinuity, resting on Selah plus the absence of a refrain sentence, which leaves 1 positive signal carrying the seam and it is one the campaign forbids as a driver.
challenges.evidence: Both close-seam signals in the row are the Selah at web:Ps.46.3 = oshb:Ps.46.4 and the non-occurrence of the refrain after it. Selah is tier-3-like corroboration, and its distribution here cannot discriminate the seam in any case: the inventory records 3 selah verses in this psalm, at oshb:Ps.46.4, oshb:Ps.46.8 and oshb:Ps.46.12, aligning with all 3 strophe closes, so Selah marks the pattern without supplying the boundary. The tier-1 discontinuity does exist in the bytes and is not cited here: the following verse opens the river-and-city image, נָהָ֗ר פְּלָגָ֗יו יְשַׂמְּח֥וּ עִיר אֱלֹהִ֑ים (web:Ps.46.4 = oshb:Ps.46.5), a subject the preceding 3 verses do not touch. That warrant is stated on the far side of the same seam by the row spanning web:Ps.46.4-46.7 but is not installed on this one, so the shared seam is argued on 1 of its 2 sides.

reviews.reasoning: Span web:Ps.46.4-46.7 = oshb:Ps.46.5-46.8. The substance is strong, and I re-derived its byte-identity claim rather than taking it. The refrain wording quoted against oshb:Ps.46.8 collates at byte tier, the same string collates at byte tier against oshb:Ps.46.12, and the two MT verses are byte-identical to each other over their full length of 70 characters each, so the row's assertion that the refrain collates byte-identical across its 2 verse occurrences is exactly true, correctly tiered and correctly unit-named. The opening quote collates at byte tier against oshb:Ps.46.5, its gloss covers the same 5 words, and the image pivot it reports is the genuine tier-1 driver for the front seam. The device_notes are disciplined in subordinating the refrain and Selah to corroboration while letting the topic shift drive, and confidence high is earned on that basis. The defect is arithmetical, in the rejected_alternative, where the rival unit is described at the wrong size.

challenges.claim: The rejected_alternative misstates the size of the rival it rejects: extending the opening strophe through this row's refrain close yields a seven-verse WEB unit, not the six-verse unit named.
challenges.evidence: The opening strophe of this psalm runs web:Ps.46.1-46.3, which is 3 WEB verses, and this row runs web:Ps.46.4-46.7, which is 4 WEB verses; extending the former through the latter gives web:Ps.46.1-46.7, which is 7 WEB verses, not 6. The MT count agrees at 7 verses, oshb:Ps.46.2-46.8, Psalm 46 being shift+1, so the figure is not an artefact of the offset: both witnesses give 7. The parallel figure on the following row is correct, where web:Ps.46.4-46.11 is 8 WEB verses and its prose says eight, which isolates this as a local off-by-one rather than a convention difference.

reviews.reasoning: Span web:Ps.46.8-46.11 = oshb:Ps.46.9-46.12. The checkable elements hold. The opening quote collates at byte tier against oshb:Ps.46.9; it is a genuine imperative pair, both forms plural, and its gloss covers the same 4 words with nothing added or dropped, so the address shift driving the front seam is demonstrated by the bytes actually quoted. The refrain quote collates at byte tier against oshb:Ps.46.12. The ordinal claim that this is the refrain's second occurrence byte-settles before it is asserted: the refrain stands at oshb:Ps.46.8 and oshb:Ps.46.12 and nowhere else in the psalm, so 46.12 is the second of 2 verse occurrences. Both selah citations check against the inventory, which records selah at oshb:Ps.46.8 and oshb:Ps.46.12 among this psalm's 3 selah verses, and both are dual-cited with correct shift+1 arithmetic. The rejected_alternative's eight-verse figure is correct, web:Ps.46.4-46.11 being 8 WEB verses. The device_notes place the driver on the imperative address shift and demote the refrain to corroboration, which is the correct weighting, and confidence high is earned by a tier-1 speech-frame shift rather than by the Selah at the seam.

Span web:Ps.47.1-47.4 = oshb:Ps.47.2-47.5, with the title pairing web:Ps.47.0 = oshb:Ps.47.1 correct for this shift+1 psalm, and the 2 superscription labels named in the device_notes both present in the inventory. The structural reading is right and the handling of the psalm seam is exemplary: the row explicitly disclaims the preceding psalm's closing Selah and refrain as evidence for this psalm's own boundary, which is the correct treatment of a separate parent composition. The close at web:Ps.47.4 is warranted by a stated tier-1 shift from summons to narrative report, with the Selah at web:Ps.47.4 = oshb:Ps.47.5 as corroboration rather than driver, and that same seam warrant is installed on the far side by the row spanning web:Ps.47.5-47.9, so the seam pair is argued symmetrically. The quote collates at byte tier and the imperative claim is correct on the pointed form. The defect is that the gloss and the quote do not cover the same span, in either direction.

challenges.claim: The opening signal's gloss neither covers nor is covered by its Hebrew quote: it drops a word that is inside the quote and renders a word that is outside it.
challenges.evidence: The quoted span is כָּֽל הָ֭עַמִּים תִּקְעוּ (web:Ps.47.1 = oshb:Ps.47.2), which collates at byte tier and is words 1-3 of an 8-word verse. The gloss reads ‘the peoples, strike the palm’. Word 1 of the quote, כָּֽל, is unrendered in that gloss; and the palm the gloss renders is word 4, כָ֑ף (web:Ps.47.1 = oshb:Ps.47.2), which lies outside the quoted span. The WEB rendering of the same verse carries both elements, “Oh clap your hands, all you nations.” (web:Ps.47.1), so the shortfall is in the row's gloss rather than in the witnesses. Extending the quote by 1 word or re-cutting the gloss to the 3 quoted words would resolve it; truncating byte-true Hebrew to fit a gloss is the regression to avoid.

reviews.reasoning: Span web:Ps.47.5-47.9 = oshb:Ps.47.6-47.10, closing the psalm; the refs arithmetic checks out, including the final verse pairing web:Ps.47.9 = oshb:Ps.47.10. The front-seam warrant is sound and agrees with its partner across the seam: the opening quote collates at byte tier against oshb:Ps.47.6, its gloss covers the same 3 words, and the turn from imperative summons to third-person narrative report is visible in the bytes quoted. The rejected_alternative is a real rival, properly rejected on scene continuity rather than taste. The second signal is where the row goes wrong, on both the count and the gloss. As an observation not filed separately: the device_notes name web:Ps.47.8 as ‘this strophe's close’ while the span closes at web:Ps.47.9, whose gathering of the princes the rationale itself reports; the substantive point that this is a structural climax and not a book-boundary doxology is correct, Book II's doxology standing at oshb:Ps.72.18-19.

challenges.claim: The count ‘occurs four times within one verse’ is predicated of a three-word quoted phrase that occurs once in the verse; the fourfold recurrence holds of 1 token, across 4 distinct pointed spellings, at a tier the row does not name.
challenges.evidence: The quoted string is זַמְּר֣וּ אֱלֹהִ֣ים זַמֵּ֑רוּ (web:Ps.47.6 = oshb:Ps.47.7), which collates at byte tier and occurs 1 time in that verse, not 4. The verse has 6 words, of which 4 share the consonantal skeleton of the imperative; those 4 tokens are זַמְּר֣וּ, זַמֵּ֑רוּ, זַמְּר֖וּ and זַמֵּֽרוּ (all web:Ps.47.6 = oshb:Ps.47.7), which are 4 distinct accented spellings with 0 byte-identical pairs among them, reducing to 2 vocalization patterns once cantillation is set aside. The fourfold repetition therefore holds of the token at skeleton tier and blends 2 spellings under one count. The swept object is not named as token rather than phrase, the tier is not named, and the figure is spelled rather than given as a digit.

challenges.claim: The same signal's gloss under-covers its quote, rendering 2 of the 3 quoted words and dropping the middle one.
challenges.evidence: The quote זַמְּר֣וּ אֱלֹהִ֣ים זַמֵּ֑רוּ (web:Ps.47.6 = oshb:Ps.47.7) is 3 words, but the gloss ‘sing praises, sing praises’ renders 2 of them and drops word 2, אֱלֹהִ֣ים (web:Ps.47.6 = oshb:Ps.47.7), the object of the opening imperative. The WEB rendering carries that object, “Sing praises to God! Sing praises! Sing praises to our King! Sing praises!” (web:Ps.47.6), so the omission is the row's. Re-cutting the gloss to the 3 quoted words is the cure; shortening the quote instead would not be.
